- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows strong upward momentum after a recent dip, check for lag: true price often peaks 1–2 days later than forecast.
- In cases of high sentiment volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days.
- When true price deviates significantly from forecast mid-horizon (e.g., 10–15% error), check if sentiment was neutral or bearish — model may be overconfident; apply downward bias of 3–7% for bearish sentiment.
- If forecast shows sharp upward correction after a spike, true price often rebounds — model may be underestimating mean reversion; adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, model often overcorrects upward — apply downward bias of 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
